findings.claim: The objective is final predicted target affinity primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; coordinate contrasts are proxies, not affinity measurements.
The learning/control support is the score-clock window [0.0, 0.5] with 50 observed score nodes at 0.01 spacing; curve support is [0.0, 0.49], so no extrapolation beyond observed nodes is licensed.

The landmark_00_soft_mass curve over [0.0, 0.49] rises from about -0.37 z early to a mid-window peak near +1.6 z around t=0.16, then declines to about -0.28 z at the last node, with 4 sign changes and polynomial_accepted=false; this is a changing contrast, not a stationary target.
Across all 20 landmark soft-mass trend rows the whole-window z is small (|z| < 0.65) and no polynomial is accepted, so no landmark soft-mass feature shows a stable monotone whole-window trend.

Strong sign conflicts are widespread (e.g. 17 for landmark_15_soft_mass, 14 for landmark_09_soft_mass, 11 for landmark_04_soft_mass), indicating batch-level disagreement rather than a reproducible regional direction.

hypotheses.direction: no directional claim; test staged relevance only
hypotheses.falsifier: a landmark soft-mass feature with polynomial_accepted=true and a stable same-sign whole-window z across independent batches
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass z-curve over observed score nodes, plus whole-window z and polynomial_accepted across landmarks
hypotheses.statement: Landmark soft-mass coordinates show no reproducible whole-window monotone target; the observed landmark_00_soft_mass curve is non-monotone with an interior peak and sign reversal, so any staged reward should be tested as a smooth time-dependent relevance schedule rather than a fixed absolute coordinate target.

hypotheses.direction: retain gradual schedule; do not introduce a hard knot
hypotheses.falsifier: a landmark with consistent same-sign first and last rates and zero sign changes across batches
hypotheses.observable: first_rate_z vs last_rate_z and sign_changes per landmark soft-mass feature
hypotheses.scope: landmarks with large |first_rate_z| or |last_rate_z| and sign_changes >= 4
hypotheses.statement: Early-window rate magnitudes are large and frequently reverse sign by the last node (landmark_00_soft_mass first_rate_z=+9.27, last_rate_z=-10.00), so an early-only or late-only teacher weighting is not supported by a stable slope; gradual change should be retained unless an independently stable knot is found.

limitations: Stage profiles and temporal profiles are unavailable; only continuous curves and trend tables were inspected.
No decoded final affinity labels are present in the delivered evidence; selection/survival and coordinate contrasts are not final-benefit measurements.
Coordinate features are untyped predicted-endpoint world-coordinate proxies; no energy or chemical-interaction interpretation is made.
Only soft-mass features were read; local covariance and displacement features were not inspected in this turn.
